learn.hook: Is your home full of cousins, or is it just you and your parents? Every family is special!
points: A family is a group of people who live together, love each other and look after each other.
A small family may have only parents and their children.
A big joint family may have grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins living together.
Some children live with one parent, or with grandparents. These are loving families too.
We have special names for relatives, like dadi, nani, chacha, mama, bua and mausi.

example.q: Kabir lives with his mother, father, dadi, dadu, chacha, chachi and two cousins. What kind of family is this?
steps: Count who lives in the home: parents, grandparents, an uncle, an aunt and cousins.
Many relatives from different generations live together under one roof.
A family like this is called a joint family.

learn.reallife: At a family wedding or a festival you may meet many relatives at once. Ask an elder to tell you how each one is related to you!

games.title: Small or joint family?
items: Ammi, Abbu and their two children
Mummy, Papa and Riya
Papa, Ma, baby Tara and Dev
A child living with parents only
Parents, children, dadi and dadu, all in one home
Two brothers, their wives and all their children together
Grandparents, uncle, aunt and cousins sharing a home
Three generations living under one roof

quiz.q: Meena lives with her mother, father and little brother. What kind of family is this?
quiz.explain: Parents and their children living together make a small family.
steps: Meena lives with her parents and her brother.
Parents and their children make a small family.
So it is a small family.
Answer: A small family
quiz.mistake: Thinks a family must have many members

quiz.q: Who is your mother's brother?
quiz.explain: Your mother's brother is your mama. Your father's younger brother is your chacha.
steps: Your mother's brother is called mama.
Your father's younger brother is chacha.
So the answer is mama.
Answer: Mama
quiz.mistake: Mixes up mother's side and father's side relatives

quiz.q: Who is your father's mother?
quiz.explain: Your father's mother is your dadi. Your mother's mother is your nani.
steps: Your father's mother is dadi.
Your mother's mother is nani.
So the answer is dadi.
Answer: Dadi
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dadi and nani

quiz.q: In a joint family, who usually lives together?
options: Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins
quiz.explain: A joint family has many relatives from different generations living in one home.
steps: A joint family is a big family.
Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together.
So that is who lives in a joint family.
Answer: Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins
quiz.mistake: Confuses a joint family with a small family

quiz.q: Aman lives with his nani and nana. Is this a real family?
options: Yes, people who live together and care for each other are a family
No, a family must have a mother and father
No, a family must have ten people
Only if they have a big house
quiz.explain: Families come in many shapes. Love and care make a family, not its size.
steps: A family is people who live together and care for each other.
Some children live with grandparents. These are loving families too.
So yes, it is a real family.
Answer: Yes, people who live together and care for each other are a family
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one correct kind of family

quiz.q: Your bua is your father's ___.
quiz.explain: Bua is the name for your father's sister.
steps: Bua is the name for your father's sister.
So the answer is sister.
Answer: Sister
quiz.mistake: Mixes up bua with chacha

quiz.q: Which of these is a good thing about living in a joint family?
options: You never have to help anyone
There are many people to share work and stories with
There is no one to play with
quiz.explain: In a joint family, many hands share the work, and children get to hear stories from grandparents.
steps: A joint family has many people in one home.
They share work and stories together.
So the good thing is having many people to share with.
Answer: There are many people to share work and stories with
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big family means less help and company

quiz.q: Two new babies are born in Pooja's small family of 3. How many people are in her family now?
quiz.explain: There were 3 people. 2 babies joined. 3 + 2 = 5.
steps: Start with 3 people
Add 2 babies: 3 + 2 = 5
Answer: 5
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the new members

teach.ask: Gappu lives only with his mama bird. He asks: is that a real family? What is a family?
teach.praise: Tweet! So my nest is a real family too. Thank you!
teach.nudge: But do all families have the same number of people?

revise.summary: A family is people who live together, love and look after each other. Families can be small, big joint families, or children living with one parent or grandparents.
focus: Every kind of family is a real family
remember: Small family: parents and their children
Joint family: grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together
Mama = mother's brother; bua = father's sister; dadi = father's mother; nani = mother's mother
traps: Don't mix up mama (mother's brother) and chacha (father's brother).
A family does not need many people; love and care make a family.

learn.hook: Dadi's stories are the best! But who helps Dadi when her knees hurt?
points: Elders are older people like grandparents. They have lots of love and lots of stories.
As people grow old, they may walk slowly, see less clearly or forget things.
We can help them: fetch their glasses, read to them, or walk slowly beside them.
Spending time and talking with elders makes them happy.
We show respect by speaking politely and listening to them.

example.q: Nanu's glasses are in the next room and he wants to read the newspaper. What can Asha do?
steps: Think: Nanu needs glasses to read, and walking is hard for him.
Asha can bring the glasses to him.
She can also offer to read the news aloud with him.
example.answer: Bring Nanu his glasses, or read the newspaper aloud to him

learn.reallife: When your grandparents visit or call, tell them about your school day. They love hearing from you!

games.title: Kind or not?
items: Walking slowly with Dadi so she does not have to hurry is kind.
Matching her speed keeps her safe and comfortable.
Laughing when Nanu forgets a name is a good way to help.
Laughing can hurt his feelings. We can gently remind him instead.
Reading a story aloud to a grandparent is a way to spend time together.
Reading together is fun and helps elders who find small print hard to see.
Elders can teach us games, songs and recipes.
Elders know many old games, songs and family recipes.
Shouting at elders shows respect.
Respect means speaking politely and calmly.
Helping Dadu remember his medicine time is a caring thing to do.
Elders may forget, so a gentle reminder helps them stay healthy.

items.text: Bring Nani her ___ so she can read.
Walk ___ with Dadu when you go to the park.

quiz.q: Dadi finds it hard to climb stairs. How can you help?
options: Hold her hand and go up slowly with her
Run up and leave her behind
quiz.explain: Walking slowly beside her and giving a hand keeps her safe.
steps: Dadi walks slowly on stairs.
We can walk slowly beside her and hold her hand.
So hold her hand and go up slowly with her.
Answer: Hold her hand and go up slowly with her
quiz.mistake: Thinks hurrying elders is helpful

quiz.q: Nana wants to talk about his childhood. What should Ravi do?
quiz.explain: Listening shows love and respect. Elders' stories also teach us about the past.
steps: Elders have lots of stories.
Listening to them shows love and respect.
So Ravi should sit with him and listen.
Answer: Sit with him and listen
quiz.mistake: Does not see listening as a way of caring

quiz.q: Why might elders need help with small things?
options: Elders do not like to do anything
As people grow old, their bodies can become weaker
quiz.explain: Old age can make eyes, knees and memory weaker, so small tasks may become hard.
steps: As people grow old, they may walk slowly, see less or forget.
Their bodies can become weaker.
So elders may need help with small things.
Answer: As people grow old, their bodies can become weaker
quiz.mistake: Blames elders instead of understanding old age

quiz.q: Which of these shows respect for elders?
quiz.explain: Greeting elders politely, like saying namaste, shows respect.
steps: We show respect by speaking politely.
Greeting elders, like saying namaste, is polite.
So greeting them politely shows respect.
Answer: Greeting them politely
quiz.mistake: Confuses rude actions with respectful ones

quiz.q: Nani often forgets to drink water. What is a caring idea?
options: Remind her gently and bring her a glass of water
quiz.explain: A gentle reminder helps her stay healthy without hurting her feelings.
steps: Nani forgets to drink water.
A gentle reminder and a glass of water help her.
So remind her gently and bring her water.
Answer: Remind her gently and bring her a glass of water
quiz.mistake: Thinks scolding is the same as helping

quiz.q: What can grandparents teach us?
options: Old stories, songs and family recipes
quiz.explain: Elders have lived a long life and know many stories, songs and recipes.
steps: Elders have lived a long life.
They know old stories, songs and recipes.
So they can teach us these.
Answer: Old stories, songs and family recipes
quiz.mistake: Thinks elders have nothing to share

quiz.q: Dadu lives in another city. How can Sana stay close to him?
options: Call him and tell him about her day
quiz.explain: Phone calls, letters and visits keep us close to elders who live far away.
steps: Dadu lives far away.
Phone calls keep us close.
So Sana can call him and tell him about her day.
Answer: Call him and tell him about her day
quiz.mistake: Thinks caring is only possible when living together

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a kind way to help an elder?
options: Helping them cross a road with an adult
Taking away their walking stick for fun
quiz.explain: A walking stick helps elders balance. Taking it away could make them fall.
steps: Carrying bags and reading labels are kind ways to help.
A walking stick helps an elder balance.
Taking it away could make them fall, so that is NOT kind.
Answer: Taking away their walking stick for fun
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the elder's safety

teach.ask: Gappu's grandpa bird is getting old and slow. Gappu asks: how can I take care of him?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will help Grandpa and listen to his stories every day!
teach.nudge: How should I talk to Grandpa so he feels respected?

revise.summary: Elders like grandparents have lots of love and stories. As they grow old they may need help, so we help them, spend time with them and speak politely.
focus: Showing respect and staying close to elders
remember: Old age can make eyes, knees and memory weaker
Help: fetch glasses, read to them, walk slowly beside them
Respect: speak politely, greet them and listen
traps: Elders are not lazy; their bodies may become weaker.
Never take away an elder's walking stick.

learn.hook: What makes a friend a good friend? Is it sharing laddoos? Maybe!
points: Friends play together, share things and help each other.
Good friends take turns, say sorry when they make a mistake and forgive each other.
Friends can be different from us. They may speak another language or like other games.
Including a new child in your game is a kind thing to do.
Friends cheer for each other and feel happy for each other.

example.q: A new girl, Lhamo, has joined your class from Sikkim. She sits alone at lunch. What can you do?
steps: Think: being new can feel lonely.
You can smile, say hello and ask her name.
Invite her to sit with your group and play at break.
example.answer: Say hello, ask her name and invite her to join you

learn.reallife: At school, in the park or in your colony, a kind word can start a new friendship.

games.title: Good friend or not?
items: Shares crayons
Says sorry after a mistake
Takes turns on the swing
Helps when you fall
Grabs your toy without asking
Laughs when you get hurt
Never lets others play
Breaks a promise on purpose

games.title: Friendship facts
items: Good friends take turns.
Taking turns is fair, so everyone gets a chance.
A friend must speak the same language as you.
Friends can speak different languages and learn from each other.
Saying sorry after a mistake helps a friendship.
It shows you care about your friend's feelings.
Leaving a new child out of every game is kind.
Inviting a new child to play is the kind thing to do.
Friends feel happy when the other one does well.
Good friends cheer for each other.

quiz.q: Arjun and Imran both want the swing. What should they do?
quiz.explain: Taking turns is fair. Both friends get to enjoy the swing.
steps: Both want the swing.
Good friends take turns.
So they should take turns.
Answer: Take turns
quiz.mistake: Thinks the strongest child should get it

quiz.q: You broke your friend's pencil by mistake. What should you say?
quiz.explain: Saying sorry shows you care about your friend's feelings.
steps: You broke the pencil by mistake.
Good friends say sorry when they make a mistake.
So say 'Sorry, it was a mistake'.
Answer: Sorry, it was a mistake
quiz.mistake: Thinks hiding a mistake is better than owning it

quiz.q: Which of these is a good friend?
options: Someone who teases you all the time
Someone who helps you when you are sad
Someone who tells lies about you
quiz.explain: A good friend is kind and helps you when you need it.
steps: Good friends help each other.
Teasing, not sharing and lying are not friendly.
So a good friend helps you when you are sad.
Answer: Someone who helps you when you are sad
quiz.mistake: Does not know what makes someone a good friend

quiz.q: A new boy who speaks Tamil joins your class. You speak Hindi. Can you be friends?
options: No, friends must speak the same language
Yes, friends can speak different languages
quiz.explain: Friendship is about kindness. You can even teach each other words in your languages!
steps: Friends can be different from us.
They may speak another language.
So yes, you can be friends.
Answer: Yes, friends can speak different languages
quiz.mistake: Thinks friends must be the same as us

quiz.q: Your friend wins the drawing contest. What is a friendly thing to do?
options: Say it was a bad drawing
quiz.explain: Good friends are happy for each other's success.
steps: Friends feel happy for each other.
Clapping and saying well done shows this.
So clap and say well done.
Answer: Clap and say well done
quiz.mistake: Feels jealous instead of happy

quiz.q: Your friend forgot his tiffin. What can you do?
options: Eat in front of him and laugh
Share some of your food with him
quiz.explain: Sharing food when a friend has none is a caring thing to do.
steps: Friends share things.
Your friend has no food.
So share some of your food with him.
Answer: Share some of your food with him
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how the friend feels

quiz.q: Your friend shares a secret about a surprise party. What should you do?
options: Keep the surprise until the party
quiz.explain: Friends trust each other. Keeping a happy surprise secret shows you are trustworthy.
steps: Friends trust each other.
A happy surprise should stay secret.
So keep the surprise until the party.
Answer: Keep the surprise until the party
quiz.mistake: Does not value trust in friendship

quiz.q: Riya has 6 toffees. She shares them equally with her friend Neha. How many toffees does each girl get?
quiz.explain: 6 toffees shared equally between 2 girls is 3 each.
steps: 2 girls share 6 toffees
6 ÷ 2 = 3 each
Answer: 3
quiz.mistake: Gives all toffees to one person instead of sharing equally

teach.ask: Gappu wants a new friend at the bird school. He asks: how can I be a good friend?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! I will share my seeds and take turns on the branch!
teach.nudge: What should I say if I hurt my friend by mistake?

revise.summary: Friends play, share and help each other. Good friends take turns, say sorry, forgive, include new children and feel happy for each other.
focus: Making friends with children who are different
Being kind to a new child
remember: Say sorry when you make a mistake, and forgive
Friends can speak other languages or like other games
traps: Friends do not have to speak the same language.
A friend who teases you all the time is not a good friend.
